practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of granting collective privileges to each House of Parliament?
opts: To grant superior legal status to Members of Parliament over ordinary citizens
To enable the House to function effectively without interference
To exempt parliamentarians from paying income taxes
To allow Parliament to amend any part of the Constitution without judicial review
practiceQuestions.sol: Collective privileges are special rights enjoyed by each House of Parliament as a body to protect its authority, dignity, and independence so it can function effectively without outside interference.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding the powers, privileges, and immunities of Parliament and its members?
opts: Article 102
Article 105
Article 110
Article 122
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 105 of the Constitution specifically deals with the powers, privileges, and immunities of Parliament, its committees, and its members.

practiceQuestions.q: The power of the House to publish debates, reports, and proceedings and to prohibit others from publishing them is derived from which constitutional or legal source?
opts: Right to Freedom of Press under Article 19(1)(a)
The Right to Information Act, 2005
The right to publish its proceedings and prohibit others from publishing them, part of collective privileges
Official Secrets Act, 1923
practiceQuestions.sol: Each House of Parliament has the collective privilege to publish its reports, debates, and proceedings, and conversely, to prohibit others from publishing the same without authorization.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a House of Parliament exclude strangers (non-members/visitors) from its proceedings at any time?
opts: No, proceedings must be open to the public at all times under Article 19
Yes, the House has the right to exclude strangers and hold secret sittings
Only the Speaker of Lok Sabha can do so, not the Rajya Sabha
Yes, but only with prior written permission from the Supreme Court
practiceQuestions.sol: A key collective privilege of each House is the right to exclude strangers (non-members) and hold secret sittings to discuss important or sensitive matters.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies is primarily responsible for examining cases of breach of privilege in the Lok Sabha?
opts: Privileges Committee
Estimates Committee
Public Accounts Committee
Business Advisory Committee
practiceQuestions.sol: The Privileges Committee in each House (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) examines every question of privilege referred to it and makes recommendations.

practiceQuestions.q: Does a House of Parliament have the right to regulate its own internal procedure and conduct of business?
opts: No, procedure is strictly laid down by the Supreme Court
Yes, each House has the right to make rules to regulate its procedure and conduct of business
Only the Union Cabinet can decide how Parliament conducts business
No, rules must be approved by a referendum of citizens
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 118, each House of Parliament may make rules for regulating its procedure and the conduct of its business, reflecting its collective autonomy.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT a collective privilege of the House of Parliament?
opts: Right to punish members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt of the House
Freedom of speech in Parliament for members
Right to receive information of arrest, detention, conviction, etc., of a member
Right to regulate its internal proceedings and to adjudicate upon matters arising within its four walls
practiceQuestions.sol: Freedom of speech in Parliament is an individual privilege of the members (though it protects the House's deliberations), while punishing for contempt, regulating internal proceedings, and receiving arrest notices are classic collective privileges.

practiceQuestions.q: What action can the House take against individuals who commit a breach of its privileges or contempt?
opts: It can only refer them to the International Court of Justice
It can reprimand, admonish, or imprison them (for the duration of the session)
It can confiscate all personal properties of the offender permanently
It has no power to penalize outsiders, only members
practiceQuestions.sol: The House has the power to punish individuals (both members and outsiders) for breach of its privileges or contempt by reprimand, admonition, or imprisonment.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 122, courts are prohibited from inquiring into the proceedings of Parliament on the ground of:
opts: Any alleged irregularity of procedure
Any violation of Fundamental Rights by a statute passed
Lack of assent from the Prime Minister
The financial cost incurred in running the session
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 122 explicitly states that the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

practiceQuestions.q: Which authority in India determines the exact scope of parliamentary privileges, as the Constitution does not codify them exhaustively?
opts: The Law Commission of India
British House of Commons conventions
United Nations General Assembly resolutions
The NITI Aayog governing council
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 105(3) stated that until defined by Parliament, the privileges of each House shall be those of the British House of Commons at the time of commencement of the Constitution (though 44th Amendment modified the reference text, British precedents heavily inform Indian parliamentary practice).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the principle of 'Exclusive Cognizance' of internal proceedings safeguard the independence of the legislature from the judiciary?
opts: By preventing courts from interfering in procedural matters and internal management of the House
By allowing the legislature to appoint and dismiss Supreme Court judges directly
By exempting all legislative acts from judicial review under all circumstances
By giving MPs immunity from civil suits arising from their private business contracts
practiceQuestions.sol: Exclusive cognizance ensures that each House has sole jurisdiction over its internal proceedings, debates, and discipline, ensuring courts cannot meddle in how Parliament conducts its internal business.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication of the phrase 'until parliament otherwise provides' under Article 105(3) regarding parliamentary privileges?
opts: Parliament is permanently barred from passing any law on privileges
It empowers Parliament to enact legislation to codify its privileges at its discretion
It makes British law permanently binding on the Indian Parliament
It gives the President sole authority to modify privileges via ordinances
practiceQuestions.sol: The phrase signifies that the constitutional framers left the door open for the Indian Parliament to codify its privileges through ordinary legislation whenever it chose to, though Parliament has chosen not to codify them comprehensively so far.

practiceQuestions.q: Why have Indian legislatures historically avoided a complete statutory codification of parliamentary privileges?
opts: Codification would subject privileges to judicial scrutiny, potentially reducing the absolute flexibility and protective scope of the House
The Constitution expressly bans any drafting of privilege laws by Parliament
Codification is too expensive for the national exchequer
British authorities legally prohibited India from altering these privileges after 1950
practiceQuestions.sol: If privileges are codified, they would become subject to Fundamental Rights and judicial review. By keeping them uncodified, the Houses retain flexible penal powers and autonomy to judge contempt.

practiceQuestions.q: In case of a conflict between Fundamental Rights (such as Article 19 or 21) and Parliamentary Privileges under Article 105, how does Indian jurisprudence generally resolve it?
opts: Fundamental Rights always override parliamentary privileges without exception
Parliamentary privileges under Article 105(3) are co-equal with Fundamental Rights, requiring harmonisation and harmonious construction
The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction whatsoever if a privilege is invoked
The President decides which provision prevails through an executive order
practiceQuestions.sol: In landmark rulings like the *Keshav Singh Case* (Special Reference No. 1 of 1964), the Supreme Court held that Article 105(3) is subject to fundamental rights, and a harmonious construction must be applied, though Parliament's core internal management remains protected.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the exact constitutional status of the privileges enjoyed by Indian parliamentary committees compared to the House itself?
opts: Committees possess zero privileges; privileges apply only when the full House sits
Committees enjoy the exact same powers, privileges, and immunities as the House as they are extensions of the House
Committees have judicial powers superior to the High Courts
Committee privileges require separate ratification by the Union Cabinet
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 105 explicitly extends privileges, powers, and immunities to parliamentary committees and their members just as it does for the House.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the collective privilege of 'prohibiting publication of proceedings' interact with modern media and live telecasts?
opts: Live telecast is completely banned by the Constitution
The House permits telecasts and reports under its own authority, retaining the right to prohibit or expunge malafide/unauthorized reporting
Media outlets have absolute constitutional immunity to broadcast anything said in the House without House regulation
All media broadcasts must be pre-censored by the Supreme Court registry
practiceQuestions.sol: While Houses authorize live telecasts (Sansad TV) and reporting (under Parliamentary Proceedings Protection Act, 1956), the underlying collective privilege gives the House the final right to control what is published, expunge remarks, and ban malicious reporting.

practiceQuestions.q: If a person is imprisoned by a House of Parliament for breach of privilege, can a court release them under a writ of Habeas Corpus?
opts: Yes, courts can always override legislative imprisonment without exception
No, if the warrant of commitment issued by the House is general (does not specify details), courts generally decline to interfere due to exclusive cognizance
Habeas corpus is exclusively applicable to legislative imprisonments only
The Prime Minister must personally countersign the habeas corpus petition
practiceQuestions.sol: Under established jurisprudence (e.g., *Gunupati Keshavram v. Nafisul Hasan* and subsequent nuances), if a House commits someone for contempt with a general warrant, courts are traditionally reluctant to inquire into the grounds under habeas corpus, upholding legislative autonomy.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are collective privileges considered essential for the dignity of Parliament in a parliamentary democracy?
opts: They ensure the executive cannot dissolve Parliament arbitrarily
They protect the collective body from public criticism and opposition protests
They shield the legislature from external pressure, intimidation, and obstruction, maintaining public faith in democratic institutions
They provide financial bonuses to MPs during economic recessions
practiceQuestions.sol: Collective privileges ensure that Parliament as an institution can deliberate free from threats, intimidation, or contempt, thus upholding the dignity and supreme legislative authority required in a democracy.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the role of the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman) when a notice of breach of privilege is moved in the House?
opts: The Presiding Officer acts as the sole judge and awards life imprisonment instantly
The Presiding Officer first examines the notice to check if a prima facie case exists before withholding or granting consent
The Presiding Officer must forward the notice directly to the Supreme Court for disposal
The Presiding Officer has no role; the matter is automatically debated without vetting
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker or Chairman is the first line of scrutiny for privilege motions. They examine whether a prima facie case of breach of privilege exists. If consented to, it is either referred to the Privileges Committee or taken up by the House.

practiceQuestions.q: How do collective privileges apply to the state legislatures under the Indian Constitution?
opts: They apply to state legislatures via Article 194, mirroring the privileges of Parliament under Article 105
State legislatures do not possess any collective privileges; only Parliament does
State privileges are decided entirely by the respective Governors on a daily basis
State privileges apply only if approved by a two-thirds majority in Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 194 of the Constitution grants analogous powers, privileges, and immunities to State Legislatures, their committees, and their members, matching those provided to Parliament under Article 105.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the collective privileges of Parliament:
1. Each House of Parliament has the right to regulate its own internal procedure and conduct of business without interference from courts.
2. The power to punish members or outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt of the House is an exclusive collective privilege.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 118 grants internal procedural autonomy, and the power to punish for contempt is a core collective privilege protecting the dignity of each House.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the publication of parliamentary proceedings:
1. Each House has the collective privilege to publish its own reports, debates, and proceedings.
2. Newspapers have an absolute, unconditional right to publish truthful reports of parliamentary proceedings without any exceptions or power of the House to prohibit it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Each House has the right to publish proceedings and prohibit others from publishing them. Statement 2 is incorrect because while the Parliamentary Proceedings (Protection of Publication) Act 1956 gives qualified protection for substantially true reports, the House retains the right to prohibit publication of its proceedings or hold secret sittings.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the right to exclude strangers:
1. Strangers include non-members, visitors, and press personnel.
2. The House can order strangers to withdraw at any time and hold secret sittings where no outsider is allowed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Strangers refer to anyone who is not a member or officer of the House. Each House possesses the collective right to exclude strangers from its chamber at any time and hold secret sittings.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 122 of the Constitution:
1. It bars courts from inquiring into any proceedings of Parliament on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure.
2. It prevents officers and members of Parliament from exercising their powers in accordance with parliamentary rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (exact wording of Article 122(1)). Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 122(2) actually protects officers and members from court jurisdiction regarding the exercise of powers vested in them for regulating procedure or conducting business.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the codification of parliamentary privileges in India:
1. The Indian Parliament has enacted a comprehensive, exhaustive statute codifying all privileges of the House and its members.
2. In the absence of a comprehensive codification statute, Indian courts refer to the traditions and precedents of the British House of Commons as incorporated via Article 105(3).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Parliament has notably never enacted a comprehensive code for privileges. Statement 2 is correct: due to this lack of codification, constitutional provisions link Indian parliamentary privileges to those of the British House of Commons.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Privileges Committee in Parliament:
壤1. It is a standing committee consisting of members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha in a joint capacity.
2. Its primary function is to examine every question of privilege referred to it by the House or the Presiding Officer and submit recommendations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because there is no joint Privileges Committee; Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have separate Privileges Committees (Lok Sabha committee has 15 members; Rajya Sabha has 10 members). Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the interaction between Fundamental Rights and Parliamentary Privileges:
1. The Supreme Court has ruled that Article 105(3) is subject to the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
2. Despite being subject to Fundamental Rights, the internal autonomy of the House to manage its proceedings without judicial interference remains protected under harmonious construction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. In the Presidential Reference (1964), the Supreme Court established that privileges must yield to Fundamental Rights when they conflict, but simultaneously upheld the exclusive jurisdiction of the House over its internal management.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding arrest or detention notices received by the House:
1. The House has the collective right to receive immediate information regarding the arrest, detention, conviction, or imprisonment of any of its members.
2. This information must be sent by the executive authorities to the President of India rather than the Presiding Officer of the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: receiving information on member arrests is a vital collective privilege. Statement 2 is incorrect because the authorities must communicate this directly to the Presiding Officer (Speaker or Chairman), not the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 and parliamentary privileges:
1. It amended Article 105(3) to remove the direct reference to the British House of Commons.
2. Instead, it substituted the reference to state that the privileges of a House shall be those of the House of Commons as it existed immediately before the coming into force of this amendment section.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 44th Amendment modified Article 105(3) so that Indian parliamentary privileges would no longer dynamically evolve with future changes in the British House of Commons, freezing the benchmark reference to the position existing at the time of the 44th Amendment (June 20, 1979).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding breach of privilege and contempt of the House:
1. Any act or omission which obstructs either House of Parliament, its members, or its officers in the performance of their functions constitutes contempt of the House.
2. Breach of privilege is a specific subset of contempt that violates the recognized rights and immunities of the House or its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Contempt of the House is a broader concept encompassing any obstruction to parliamentary functioning, while breach of privilege specifically violates recognized privileges. All breaches of privilege are contempts, but not all contempts are breaches of specific privileges.
